name: Shihāb al-Dīn Abū al-ʿAbbās Aḥmad ibn Yūsuf al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
summary: Aleppan grammarian and reader who settled in Cairo; his al-Durr al-maṣūn is the fullest grammatical analysis of the Qurʾān.
bio: Al-Samīn ('the stout') came from Aleppo to Cairo, where he learnt grammar from Abū Ḥayyān and the Qurʾān readings from the masters of the city, and taught both. His al-Durr al-maṣūn fī ʿulūm al-kitāb al-maknūn analyses the Qurʾān word by word, its iʿrāb, its readings and its morphology, and often corrects his teacher's al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ. He also wrote a dictionary of the words of the Qurʾān, ʿUmdat al-ḥuffāẓ. He died in Cairo in 756/1355.
